parts.name: Parikshith Aithal K V
parts.title: Patterns, profiles and trustworthy comparisons
parts.question: Which patterns are supported by the data, and which impressions depend on how we draw or aggregate it?
parts.infovis: Network: construction, three layouts, search/selection/filtering, country trajectories and profile interpretation.
parts.scivis: Color mapping: continuous/discrete palettes, normalization, global/local extrema, global/local scalar GIFs.
parts.finding: Similar adoption can accompany different infrastructure profiles. Fixed scales and complete daily coverage distinguish measured differences from drawing or sampling effects.
parts.anchor: Figures 1-3 show layout effects, country paths and NodeTrix links; Figures 17-18 establish fair scalar comparisons; Figure 23 shows how monthly totals hide concentrated rainfall.
parts.handoff: The comparisons are now consistent. But has progress actually reduced inequality, and does an average describe the countries or places behind it?

parts.name: Sindhoor Ganapathi Hegde
parts.title: The digital divide, trajectories and hidden persistence
parts.question: Does broad progress mean convergence, and what do averages hide about individual changes and persistent conditions?
parts.infovis: Temporal methods: both horizon variations and both ridgeline variations, with their baselines, cohorts and density checks.
parts.scivis: Contour mapping: Marching Squares-family tracing, lines/fills, interval comparison and contour GIF.
parts.finding: Regional summaries hide country differences: 47% of measured 2020 variation lies within regions. Regional median shifts differ from typical individual gains. Event frequency differs from uninterrupted duration.
parts.anchor: Figures 10-12 connect timing to within-region variation and country gains; Figures 13-16 demonstrate the required temporal methods; Figure 30 distinguishes event counts from persistent runs.
parts.handoff: Progress is real but uneven, and a summary can conceal very different experiences. Which infrastructure relationships remain when we inspect the original measurements and their changes?

parts.name: Varshith M Gowda
parts.title: Infrastructure relationships, interactions and the final answer
parts.question: Which relationships survive inspection across variables, country changes and joint conditions?
parts.infovis: JavaScript browser methods: bundled parallel coordinates with brushing/reordering AND zoomable treemap with two hierarchy remodelings.
parts.scivis: Quiver: spatial sampling, proportional versus equal arrow lengths, meteorological FROM to flow TO conversion and speed key.
parts.finding: The strong broadband/adoption association across country levels does not describe matched changes. User counts and adoption shares answer different questions. Individual weather conditions are more common than their exact joint overlap.
parts.anchor: Figures 4-9 connect interactive methods to the infrastructure question; Figure 26 demonstrates the vector experiment; Figure 29 separates marginal prevalence from joint overlap.
parts.handoff: Final answer: averages hide heterogeneity, snapshots hide temporal order, and separate variables hide joint occurrence. Each conclusion depends on its stated units, cohort, scale and time support.
